prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production animation extension of an ADOPTED pixel game character, not a redesign. The attached sheet is the approved design and poses at nearest 4x; use its first standing pose as exact identity, palette, scale and proportions. Same adopted masked fat muscular pale dirty-skinned brute. Preserve the constructed dark leather full-head mask with dark goggles and dull brass snout vent, the exact wrapped chain loops around chest/belly, dark trousers and boots. Never actual pig head. Body ~46 native pixels tall.
Create only these NEW motion poses: 4 columns x 2 rows. Top row: four alternating heavy WALK phases (near foot forward, far passing, far forward, near passing), upper torso and permanently wrapped chains stable, fists low. Bottom row: (4) hit recoil hands protect chest alive, (5) recover from hit, (6) lumbering retreat step near foot forward, (7) retreat opposite foot. All facing RIGHT. Do NOT draw the separate hanging ball or extended chain; those are separate parts. Only the permanent wrapped torso chain stays.
Transparent RGBA background, equal grid cells, generous transparent gutters, consistent full-body scale and ground baseline, complete feet and limbs. Clean chunky square pixel clusters for a small game sprite enlarged into the output, same muted palette, 1-pixel native dark brown contour, upper-left illumination. No smooth airbrushed illustration, no labels/grid/text/background/ground shadows/additional people. Same head and face in every cell. Meaningful limb changes, never just translated duplicates. Output only the motion sheet.
